stimulus.source_note: Photograph: crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival, August 15, 1969. Photograph by Derek Redmond and Paul Campbell, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph, taken on August 15, 1969, shows part of the huge crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York. More than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of rock music.

stem: Woodstock in 1969 is best remembered as which moment in American culture?

options.text: The end of rock music as a popular American art form
options.misconception: Background from the books: rock kept growing after Woodstock, so the festival did not end it.

options.text: The first time teenagers listened to the radio
options.misconception: Background from the books: teenagers had listened to the radio since the 1950s, long before Woodstock.

options.text: The high point of a counterculture built on peace and music
A protest that ended the war in Vietnam
options.misconception: Background from the books: the war in Vietnam continued until 1973, so Woodstock did not end it.

rationales.A: Background from the books: rock kept growing after Woodstock, so the festival did not end it.
rationales.B: Background from the books: teenagers had listened to the radio since the 1950s, long before Woodstock.
rationales.C: Background from the books: more than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of music, the peak of the peace-and-love counterculture.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the war in Vietnam continued until 1973, so Woodstock did not end it.
rationales.general:
1. More than 400,000 young people gathered on a farm for three days of music.
2. Background from the books: the festival was the high moment of the counterculture, when the personal mattered more than the political.
3. A gathering that large, peaceful, and young is remembered as a peak, not as a beginning or an end.
Remember: A movement's high point is the moment its people gather largest and its style is most visible.
